title: Self-Simulation with Linear Space Overhead
statement: For every effective code system $c$ for one-work-tape binary machines, there is a finite-state deterministic binary machine $U_0$ such that for every code $\alpha$ there is a positive integer $C$ with the following property. For every binary input $w$, output word $y$, and natural numbers $t,s$, if the machine decoded from $\alpha$ halts on input $\langle\alpha,w\rangle$ at time $t$ with output $y$ and uses exactly $s$ work-tape cells by time $t$, then $U_0$ halts on input $\langle\alpha,w\rangle$ with output $y$ at some time $t'$ and uses at most $C(s+1)$ work-tape cells by time $t'$.
hypotheses_covered: $c$ is an effective code system for one-work-tape binary machines
$U_0$ is a finite-state deterministic binary machine
the decoded machine computes output $y$ and halts at time $t$ on paired input $\langle\alpha,w\rangle$
its space used by time $t$ is at most $s$
replaced:
For every effective code system for one-work-tape binary machines, there exist a
finite-state deterministic binary machine $U_0$ such that, for each code $\alpha$, there
is a positive integer $C$ with the following property. If the machine decoded from
$\alpha$ halts on the paired input $\langle\alpha,w\rangle$ within $t$ steps, outputs a
binary string, and uses at most $s$ work-tape cells by time $t$, then $U_0$ halts on the
same paired input with the same output at some time $t'$ and uses at most $C(s+1)$
cells.
